metadata.title: Turning the guard into the attacker: DoubleAgent, BYOVD, and AV/EDR subversion
metadata.frame: A recurring class of attack weaponizes the SECURITY PRODUCT itself - abusing legitimate OS features or signed drivers to hijack or kill antivirus/EDR. DoubleAgent (Cybellum, 2017) abuses Microsoft's Application Verifier to inject code into any process, including the AV; BYOVD (bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver) and EDR-killers load signed-but-vulnerable kernel drivers to blind endpoint defense. Same theme as the MS_Nightmare Defender exploits: the defender is the attack surface.
metadata.grade: DoubleAgent's technique, disclosure (Cybellum, Mar 2017), and affected-vendor PoC list = FACT (Cybellum; contemporaneous coverage). BYOVD as a widely-used technique + EDR-killer tooling (AuKill, EDRKillShifter) tied to ransomware crews = FACT (vendor/IR reporting). 'Most AV vendors affected' reflects the 2017 PoC scope; vendors since mitigated (PPL).
metadata.honest_limits: DoubleAgent required existing admin/code-exec to register the verifier provider - it is a persistence/injection + defense-evasion technique, not a remote break by itself. Microsoft's Protected Process Light (PPL) for AV services is the documented mitigation. BYOVD depends on a vulnerable signed driver being loadable (Microsoft's driver blocklist is the counter). Specific ransomware-crew attributions for EDR-killers are as-reported by IR vendors.
metadata.method: Cybellum DoubleAgent disclosure (Mar 2017); Microsoft Application Verifier docs + PPL; MITRE ATT&CK (defense evasion / hijack execution flow); IR vendor reporting on BYOVD + AuKill/EDRKillShifter (RansomHub).

edges.notes: DoubleAgent (Cybellum, Mar-2017) abuses Microsoft's Application Verifier - a legitimate Windows runtime-verification tool. An attacker registers a malicious 'verifier provider' DLL for a target process; Windows then loads that DLL into the process on EVERY start - persistent, pre-boot code injection into arbitrary processes (fact). Requires prior admin/code-exec (technique, not remote break).
Application Verifier ships with Windows (a developer/QA tool) - the classic 'living-off-the-land' pattern: subvert a trusted first-party feature rather than drop novel malware (fact/context).

The marquee abuse: hijack the ANTIVIRUS process itself. The 2017 PoC weaponized/neutralized most major AV/endpoint products (Avast, AVG, Avira, Bitdefender, ESET, F-Secure, Kaspersky, Malwarebytes, McAfee, Norton, Panda, Trend Micro, Comodo). Turning the guard into the attacker (fact of PoC; vendors mitigated via PPL).
The documented defense: run AV/EDR as a Protected Process Light (PPL) so non-PPL code (incl. a verifier provider) cannot inject into or tamper with the security service (fact of mitigation).

Same thread as the MS_Nightmare Defender 0-days: the endpoint SECURITY product is the target/attack surface. DoubleAgent (2017, injection/persistence) and the 2026 Defender LPE dumps are two eras of 'weaponize the guard' (interpretation).

Anchors the 'living-off-the-land / defense-evasion' branch of the lineage - abusing trusted OS mechanisms (Application Verifier, later AppInit/IFEO/COM hijacks) rather than novel exploits (fact of category).

Bring-Your-Own-Vulnerable-Driver: load a legitimately SIGNED but vulnerable kernel driver (e.g. RTCore64, various OEM drivers) to gain kernel-level execution and disable protections - the engine behind most EDR-killers (fact).

EDR-killer tooling (AuKill; EDRKillShifter, tied by IR vendors to the RansomHub ecosystem) uses BYOVD to terminate/blind AV/EDR agents before ransomware detonation - the modern successor to DoubleAgent's guard-hijack (fact per IR reporting; crew attributions as-reported).
Microsoft's counter is the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist (HVCI/WDAC) - but coverage lags newly-abused drivers, so BYOVD remains effective in practice (fact; efficacy graded).
The kernel-level branch of defense evasion - signed-driver abuse - now standard in ransomware playbooks; complements the user-mode DoubleAgent technique (fact of category).
